jobs.description:
At Struers, we help companies and laboratories around the world understand their materials and make confident decisions about quality. Our purpose is Ensuring Certainty, and behind the equipment that delivers that certainty is increasingly sophisticated software.

We are looking for a Software Engineer to help develop the machine-control software behind our next generation of products.

Our machine-control platform is based on modern PLC technology, but this is not a traditional PLC programming role. We approach machine control as a software engineering discipline, applying principles such as structured architecture, modularity, reuse, design patterns, automated testing, and maintainable code.

Whether your background is embedded software, automation, control engineering, C/C++, C#, or PLC development, we are interested in strong software engineers who enjoy making software interact with the physical world.

You will contribute from early concepts through product launch, developing reusable software components, machine behavior, and control algorithms, and validating your solutions directly on real machines.

Key Responsibilities:

• Implement machine control and process logic for Struers machines.

• Design control algorithms and implement software designs based on input from software architects.

• Develop and improve reusable software modules and libraries for Struers machines.

• Apply modern software engineering principles to create robust, modular, testable, and maintainable machine software.

• Test and verify software directly on real machines and equipment.

• Work closely with mechanical, hardware, and project teams.

• Participate in R&D product projects from concept phase to product launch.

• Contribute to code reviews and analysis of other developers’ work.

• Establish required design, test, and product documentation.

• Support handover of product software and documentation to the engineering department responsible for product and platform maintenance.

• Collaborate with international software colleagues, including the Czech software team.

• Demonstrate the ability and willingness to use AI tools to improve productivity, decision-making, work quality, and cost efficiency.

• Identify appropriate AI use cases and critically evaluate AI-generated outputs.

Requirements:

Education & Experience:

Must-have:

• Relevant engineering degree or similar technical background.

• Hands-on software development experience.

• Ability to develop structured and maintainable software.

• Experience from at least one relevant software development technology, for example, C/C++, C#, Java, PLC programming, or another structured or object-oriented programming language.

• Interest in automation, machine control, PLC-based systems, embedded software, or industrial software development.

• Ability and motivation to work with physical equipment and test software on real machines.

• Good communication skills in English, both spoken and written.

Nice-to-have:

• Experience with machine control, process logic, automation systems, or control/regulation.

• Experience with object-oriented programming.

• Experience with Structured Text or PLC programming.

• Experience designing or implementing control algorithms.

• Experience from industrial equipment, machinery, production equipment, or similar domains.

• Experience working in international engineering teams.

Professional skills:

• Structured and analytical approach to software development.

• Ability to understand software designs and implement them in a maintainable way.

• Ability to work close to physical products and solve practical engineering problems.

• Strong collaboration skills across software, hardware, mechanical, and project disciplines.

• Ability to take responsibility for implementation tasks within product projects.

• Interest in building robust, reusable, and maintainable software solutions.

• Good communication skills and ability to contribute positively in an international team.

• Self-motivated and focused on moving tasks toward completion.

• Curious and willing to learn Struers’ products, domain, platform, and development practices.

Success Criteria:

• High-quality machine-control software is delivered according to project needs and the agreed software architecture.

• Machine control and process logic are implemented in a structured, maintainable, and reusable way.

• Software is tested and verified systematically on real machines and equipment.

• Reusable software modules and libraries contribute to reduced development time across projects.

• Software design and implementation meet relevant quality, maintainability, cost, and compliance expectations.

• The role contributes positively to collaboration between software, mechanical, hardware, and project teams.

• The role contributes to effective collaboration across locations, including with the Czech software team.

• Product software and documentation are handed over in a structured way to the engineering department responsible for product and platform maintenance.

About the Business Unit

Struers is an AMETEK business unit and a global leader in materialographic and metallographic solutions, providing equipment, consumables, software, and services for material testing, sample preparation, and hardness testing. Its technologies help manufacturers, research institutions, and laboratories analyze materials and ensure the highest standards of quality, reliability, and performance across industries such as aerospace, automotive, electronics, energy, and advanced manufacturing.

Founded in 1875 in Denmark and headquartered in Ballerup, Denmark, Struers has more than 150 years of expertise in material science and a global presence with offices and support teams worldwide. Known for its strong application knowledge, innovation, and customer-focused approach, Struers helps organizations achieve accurate and reproducible material analysis results that support product development, quality control, and scientific advancement.

For more information, visit www.ametek.com/ and www.struers.com/en

**About Flatpay

**Flatpay is not just another payment solution; we're dedicated to innovating the market for payment solutions and financial services in the SME segment with our customer-centric and transparent services.

We've grown into one of the fastest-growing fintech companies out of the Nordics and Denmark's fastest unicorn company. Today, we're more than 2,600 colleagues across Europe, building products that make a real difference for our customers.

We're ambitious, move fast, and like to challenge the status quo - but we also believe work should be fun. We celebrate wins, help each other out, and create an environment where people can do great work while genuinely enjoying the journey.

**About The Job

**Flatpay has become one of Europe's fastest-growing payment companies by helping merchants accept card payments in-store.

Our Point of Sale system serves as the central engine of the business. It streamlines the merchant's entire workflow — from order taking, product and inventory management, to payment processing, reporting, and compliance.

**Some Of The Core Capabilities Include

**

And with our customer base doubling approximately every six months, the demands on scalability, reliability and performance continue to grow.

This is a hands-on engineering role with significant ownership. You'll influence technical direction, contribute to architectural decisions and solve the engineering challenges that come with building one of Europe's fastest-growing commerce platforms.

About Be My Eyes

Be My Eyes is on a mission to make the world more accessible for the 340 million people who are blind or have low vision. Our apps connect people with volunteers, companies and AI through live video, free of charge, so they can handle the inaccessible parts of everyday life at home and at work.

The idea came from Hans Jørgen Wiberg, a Danish craftsman with low vision. The app launched in 2015, drew 10,000 volunteer sign-ups in its first 24 hours, and now has millions of volunteers helping in more than 180 languages. Today our products include the Be My Eyes app, Be My AI, Be My Eyes for Smart Glasses, the Service Directory and Be My Eyes for Desktop.

We build products with our community, not just for it, and their needs come first even when that challenges our own assumptions. We move fast, care about the details and take ownership of what we ship. We see mistakes as part of pushing boundaries, and we take kindness seriously while keeping room for fun.

We're also working to reach the rest of the 340 million people who are blind or have low vision, wherever they live and whatever device they use. Our tools are free for the people who rely on them. We build them to improve lives, not to make a quick profit.

You will become part of a dedicated team consisting of 2 Scientists and 7 Laboratory Technicians, reporting directly to the Manager, Material Receipt. As part of the wider QC organization, collaboration is highly valued. We support each other across teams when needed, and you can therefore expect to contribute to activities such as deviation handling, ad hoc assignments, and training of colleagues outside the team.

About MicroTech Software

MicroTech is a small software company with more than 35 years of experience building custom solutions in close dialogue with our customers, mainly in banking and insurance. Since 2025, applying AI has been a major focus for us.

We value quality over quantity, and we keep the customer experience at the centre. Expect great colleagues and a busy but relaxed workday in an informal atmosphere. We also care about ESG and like to give back, for example through sponsorships and by being an inclusive workplace that welcomes employees who need special accommodations.

About the role

You’ll help shape the architecture of a live AI product running on our own on-prem LLM stack.

Two big projects are coming up, and you’ll play a key part in both:

• Voice-to-workflow: making speech a first-class input channel in our agentic workflows

• Moving to a graph architecture: going from RAG to GraphRAG by building a knowledge graph and integrating it into our existing pipeline

Responsibilities

Shape the architecture of a live AI product

• Evaluate and challenge design decisions across the stack, including retrieval strategies, LLM backend selection, service boundaries and data flow, and propose improvements with clear reasoning

• Take part in technical planning with the team and with insurance-domain stakeholders, turning vague requirements into concrete engineering tasks

• Identify technical debt, assess its cost and make the case for addressing it

Develop and optimize our on-prem AI stack

• Further develop and optimize our self-hosted LLM stack: local models, local embedding and on-prem vector stores

• Evaluate open-weight LLMs for Danish-language RAG quality, weighing latency, accuracy and hardware requirements

Move to a graph architecture (RAG → GraphRAG)

• Help design and build a knowledge graph for our domain, including ontology and knowledge extraction

• Integrate the knowledge graph into our existing RAG pipeline and measure the effect on retrieval quality

Design and build agentic workflows

• Design multi-step agent architectures using LangGraph or equivalent frameworks that can route, plan, use tools and synthesize across document corpora

• Define tool-use interfaces, memory patterns and failure-handling strategies for agent loops running in production

• Work with domain experts to identify automation opportunities worth building

Enable voice-to-workflow capabilities

• Help design a pipeline that integrates local speech-to-text models into agentic workflows

• Evaluate Danish-language ASR quality, identify gaps and assess whether fine-tuning or model selection is the better approach

• Design the integration points carefully, with attention to latency, error handling and data privacy, so voice becomes a first-class input channel

Requirements

• 2–4 years of production Python engineering experience, including async code, clean architecture patterns and testable codebases

• Direct experience with LLM orchestration frameworks (LangChain or similar) in a shipped product or serious project

• Solid understanding of RAG systems: chunking strategies, embedding models, vector search and retrieval quality evaluation

• Familiarity with vector databases such as pgvector, Chroma, Weaviate or Pinecone

• Comfortable owning a FastAPI service end-to-end: schema design, error handling, auth,

• containerization and deployment

• Ability to reason about architectural trade-offs and communicate them clearly

• Hands-on experience designing or running local LLM inference (Ollama, vLLM, llama.cpp) in a real rather than toy context

Nice to have

• Familiarity with knowledge graphs, including ontology building, knowledge extraction and RAG integration (especially relevant)

• Speech-to-text pipeline work (Whisper, Deepgram, Speechmatics or comparable local STT), especially on non-English languages (especially relevant)

• Experience with agentic frameworks (LangGraph, AutoGen, CrewAI) or custom tool-use and planning loops in production

• Hybrid retrieval systems (dense + sparse, BM25 + vector) and re-ranking with cross-encoders

• LLM observability and tracing tools (Arize Phoenix, LangSmith or similar)

• Multilingual NLP, particularly Danish or other Nordic languages

• Knowledge of regulated-industry data handling, GDPR or EU AI Act compliance

• Cloud platforms (e.g. Azure), container registries and CI/CD

What we offer

• Beautiful offices: art on the walls, plenty of green plants and high ceilings

• Great location: bus, train and light rail right outside the door, easy to reach by car, and free parking

• Flexible work: a hybrid setup with the option to work from home up to around 2 days a week after the initial onboarding

• Small organisation: very short decision-making processes and great opportunities for co-responsibility

• Personal development: varied tasks, direct client contact and support for further education

• All phases: you’ll work on everything from definition and solution design to programming and production

• Competitive salary: an attractive compensation package that matches your skills

Please note

• Start date: as soon as possible. We’ll still take the time to find the right person, so we review applications on an ongoing basis and will keep the position open until it’s filled.

• This is a hybrid role based at our office in Viby J., Aarhus. It is not a remote position.

• We cannot offer work permit sponsorship or relocation support. Applicants must already have the right to work in Denmark.

jobs.description:
Are you excited about the prospects of a career at the intersection of machine learning, materials science and autonomous robotics? Do concepts like federated self-driving laboratories (SDL), machine-learned potentials, agentic AI, FAIR workflows, and autonomous materials discovery resonate with you? Responsibilities for the two positions:

• The development of next-generation MLIPs and Hessian Interatomic Potentials (HIPs) for prediction of electrochemical reactions mechanisms and rates at solid-liquid and solid-polymer interfaces in batteries and catalysts, e.g., for in-loop deployment in agentic workflows bridging experimental and simulation-based modalities.

• The development experimental of SDL modules for synthesis and testing of sustainable battery and catalyst materials and interfaces, e.g., PFAS-free binders and electrolytes, and their implementation in agentic workflows for federated deployment of experiments and simulations.

DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

The Pioneer Center CAPeX is a 13-year and 300 MDKK “Pioneer Center for Accelerating P2X Materials Discovery”, funded by the Danish Ministry of Higher Education and Science, the Danish National Research Foundation, the Carlsberg Foundation, the Lundbeck Foundation, the Novo Nordisk Foundation, and the Villum Foundation. CAPeX is hosted by the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and co-hosted by Aalborg University (AAU) and unites leading experts from DTU, AAU, University of Copenhagen, Aarhus University, and the University of Southern Denmark with international partners from Stanford University, Utrecht University, Imperial College London, and the University of Toronto to form a truly Pioneering Center on P2X. You can read more about the CAPeX research themes and X-trails, our organization at http://www.capex.dtu.dk_._

Furthermore, our approach is fully aligned with relevant innovation strategies, policies, and programmes across Europe, ensuring coherence, scalability, and long-term impact._

BRIGHT serves as a hub for academic and industrial partners working together to unlock the potential of bioproduction. The technologies include fuel cells, electrolysis, power-to-x, batteries, and carbon capture. Read more about us at www.energy.dtu.dk_._

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829

DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. jobs.occupation: Associate Director, Quality Assurance – Drug Product & Device
jobs.description:
About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

Getting a promising treatment into a clinical trial takes more than good science. Patients need medicines and delivery devices they can rely on, made to the right standards and available when needed.

As Associate Director, QA Drug Product & Device, you'll own quality oversight of our drug product manufacturing partners and combination product development. You'll work closely with CMC, Manufacturing and device development colleagues to resolve quality risks, keep clinical supplies moving and build the quality framework Hemab needs as its pipeline advances.

What you'll do

• Ensure QA oversight of selected drug product CDMOs and fill-finish activities in collaboration with the CMC and Manufacturing team

• Ensure QA oversight of design controls and risk management for combination products, including review and approval of design control deliverables, in line with 21 CFR Part 4 and EU MDR Article 117

• QA review and approval of master and executed batch records, specifications, protocols and reports

• Oversee and manage drug product deviations, CAPAs and change controls

• Ensure batch documentation is complete and release-ready, and support the Qualified Person in the certification and release of drug product and combination product batches

• Create and review quality agreements with drug product CDMOs and suppliers

• Advise and support the CMC and Manufacturing team as quality lead for selected programs

• Participate in building and improving fit-for-purpose quality systems and processes as Hemab grows, and contribute to projects across Quality and the wider organization

What you'll bring to Hemab

• Hands-on QA experience with combination products or drug-device products, including design controls and ISO 14971 risk management

• Experience overseeing drug product CDMOs, ideally aseptic fill-finish, including audits and quality agreements

• Working knowledge of EU GMP (including Annex 1), 21 CFR Parts 210/211 and 600-610, and 21 CFR Part 4 and ISO 13485.

• A collaborative, cross-functional working style, partnering closely with CMC & Manufacturing, device development, supply chain and regulatory colleagues

• Good communication skills. English is our company language, so you are comfortable writing and speaking it professionally

• A solution-oriented and hands-on way of working, comfortable taking ownership and shaping processes as the organization evolves.

Nice to have Eligibility, or a realistic path, to act as an EU Qualified Person

• Experience with prefilled syringes, autoinjectors or other injectable delivery systems

• Danish language skills

What to expect, honestly

You'll be accountable for quality, but much of the manufacturing happens outside Hemab. That means working through CDMOs, sometimes with incomplete information, competing timelines and decisions that cannot wait. You'll need to know when to challenge, when to escalate and when there's enough evidence to move forward.

Drug product manufacturing and device development don't always move at the same pace. A late deviation, an unresolved design control issue or missing batch documentation can affect clinical supply. You'll need to get close to the detail, work directly with partners and find a compliant way forward.

Some of our quality frameworks are still being built. You'll help establish them while managing today's work. If you prefer established systems and clearly separated responsibilities, this may be frustrating. If you enjoy building sensible ways of working that protect patients without slowing good decisions, there's room to make a real difference.

Why Hemab

At Hemab, your work ultimately connects back to something simple. People living with serious bleeding disorders get something they've never had before - the chance to prevent a bleed, instead of reacting to one after it happens. You'll be joining at a stage where individual decisions still carry real weight, and where your work can help turn promising science into a preventative treatment that actually reaches patients.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty, and respect. We're still building the consistency to back that up across every hiring process, every time. We'd say that plainly instead of pretending otherwise. If any part of your experience with us falls short of it, tell us.

Hemab builds balanced candidate slates and assesses everyone against a single standard. If you need a reasonable adjustment at any stage of the hiring process, please tell us.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Hemab Therapeutics is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, seeking to create a welcoming and diverse environment. All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, sex, marital status, gender expression or identity, genetic information, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

We're adding a Clinical Trial Manager to take ownership of study delivery as our clinical portfolio grows. You'll be responsible for turning clinical development plans into well-run trials, keeping sites, CROs and internal teams focused on what matters: enrolling patients, protecting their safety and generating reliable data.

Based in Copenhagen, you'll work closely with Clinical Operations colleagues and teams across both locations. This is a hands-on role with room to shape how we run studies as Hemab grows.

What you'll do

• Take ownership of the day-to-day delivery of assigned clinical trials, from start-up through close-out, against agreed timelines, budgets and quality standards.

• Drive site activation and patient recruitment, working with investigators and CROs to identify obstacles early and find practical solutions.

• Manage CROs and external vendors, holding partners accountable for their commitments and addressing performance issues directly.

• Develop and maintain study plans, timelines and risk assessments that give the team a clear picture of progress and what needs attention.

• Work closely with Clinical Development, Medical, Regulatory, Data Management and Quality colleagues to resolve study issues and keep decisions moving.

• Oversee study budgets, forecasts and vendor expenditure, identifying potential overruns before they become problems.

• Maintain compliance with ICH-GCP, study protocols and applicable regulations, with inspection readiness built into everyday trial delivery.

• Help establish practical ways of working that can be used across studies without adding unnecessary complexity.

What you'll bring to Hemab

• Experience managing interventional clinical trials, with direct responsibility for study delivery and oversight of external partners.

• A working knowledge of clinical trial start-up, site management, recruitment, monitoring and close-out.

• Experience addressing recruitment delays, site performance issues or other challenges that threaten study timelines.

• Sound knowledge of ICH-GCP and the regulatory requirements governing clinical trials.

• Experience managing CROs, study budgets and timelines, with the judgement to know when to escalate an issue.

• The ability to work effectively with colleagues across clinical, scientific and regulatory disciplines, including when priorities change.

Nice to have

• Experience in rare diseases, haematology or coagulation.

• Experience working in a smaller biotech company or helping establish clinical trial ways of working.

• Experience with international, multicentre clinical studies.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. Systems here tend to get created as we need them, not handed down in advance. Whoever takes this role will likely build some of their own process instead of inheriting a finished one. We work across two hubs and multiple time zones - bridging that well takes real, deliberate effort. And because we're growing quickly, priorities can shift with less notice than they would at a larger, more established company.

We value people who take responsibility when something goes wrong, ask for help when needed and work without ego. At our size, how you work matters as much as where you've worked. Good structure should help people move faster and trust each other, not create more work.

Why Hemab

We are looking for a Senior Patent Attorney to play a central role in protecting and enabling innovation across Demant's global business and help shape the future of our Intellectual Property function.

In this role, you will partner closely with R&D teams, engineers, scientists, and business stakeholders to ensure that Demant continues to develop and launch innovative products with the lowest possible litigation risk. You will contribute to the growth and strengthening of our international patent portfolio while providing strategic IP guidance that supports our business ambitions.

This role requires more than technical expertise and patent law knowledge. It requires curiosity, commercial understanding, good stakeholder management, and the ability to translate complex technologies into valuable intellectual property. This is where you come in.

Welcome to Demant Intellectual Property

You will join Demant's Intellectual Property team at our Demant headquarters in Smørum, just outside Copenhagen, and become part of a highly skilled and collaborative team consisting of Patent Attorneys, Trademark Attorneys, and IP Paralegals.

Demant is a growing, world-leading hearing healthcare corporation that offers solutions in hearing devices, diagnostic instruments, and intelligent audio and video equipment. Through innovative technologies and deep expertise, we are dedicated to making life-changing differences for people with hearing loss around the world.

Our team consists of 14 colleagues from several different nationalities and professional backgrounds. We believe that results are achieved through collaboration and knowledge-sharing. We actively support one another, provide constructive feedback, and continuously develop our collective expertise in both technology and intellectual property.

Working closely with globally distributed business units and R&D organizations, our primary purpose is to help ensure that Demant's products can successfully reach the market while minimizing intellectual property risks.

Help protect the innovations of tomorrow

Joining us, you will bring an intellectual property perspective to strategic technology decisions and help researchers, engineers, and business leaders navigate an increasingly complex innovation landscape.

A key part of your role will be identifying opportunities and risks early in the development process and helping stakeholders answer critical questions: Are we free to commercialize this technology? How can we strengthen our competitive position? How can we protect our innovations globally? And how do we build an IP portfolio that supports Demant's long-term business strategy?

You will work across the boundaries of technology, law, and business, helping transform ideas into protected innovations while supporting product and technology development from concept to market launch.

In this role, you will

• Support innovation throughout the product lifecycle – Participate in R&D project groups and provide IP guidance throughout the development process and help teams make informed technology and business decisions.

• Drive freedom-to-operate activities – Conduct analyses and provide strategic advice to ensure products can be launched with the lowest possible litigation risk.

• Expand and strengthen Demant's patent portfolio – Evaluate invention disclosures, identify patentable innovations, and actively contribute to the growth of our international patent portfolio.

• Manage patent drafting and prosecution – Prepare, file, and prosecute patent applications in multiple jurisdictions while working closely with inventors and external partners.

• Analyze competitor patents – Prepare, file, and present at opposition proceedings before the European Patent Office

• Develop intellectual property expertise – Contribute to the team's collective knowledge within technology and patent law while continuously expanding your own professional capabilities.

By joining Demant, you will step into a highly visible role where your ability to connect technology, intellectual property, and business strategy will directly support innovation and help protect products that improve the lives of people across the world.

What You Bring

You have a scientific or technical background combined with practical intellectual property experience and a genuine interest in understanding how innovation creates business value.

You bring:

• Qualification as a European Patent Attorney or as a US Patent Attorney.

• 5+ years of experience within intellectual property, gained either in industry, private practice, or a combination of both.

• A scientific or technical degree, preferably within physics, electronics, or a related field.

• Excellent analytical capabilities and the ability to quickly understand new technologies and technical concepts.

• Strong communication skills and the ability to explain complex IP matters clearly to a broad range of stakeholders.

• A structured and systematic approach combined with strong attention to detail.

• An interest in understanding business needs and translating them into effective IP strategies.

Finally, you are curious, collaborative, and enjoy working closely with experts across different disciplines. You combine technical depth with commercial awareness, build trusted relationships with stakeholders, and are motivated by helping innovation succeed.

Flexible Working Conditions

At Demant, we work in a collaborative environment built on trust, openness, and strong professional relationships. Networking and knowledge-sharing are essential parts of how we work.

We offer you flexible working conditions, excellent opportunities for professional development, and a highly skilled team that works towards a common goal. From the moment you enter our premises, you will experience Demant's energizing and welcoming spirit.

Join our diverse organization and work alongside colleagues from many different nationalities and backgrounds while contributing to technologies that make a meaningful difference in people's lives.

Come and join us

Do you thrive at the intersection of technology and governance? Are you equally comfortable discussing access models with data engineers and governance frameworks with business stakeholders?

At Tryg, we're looking for a Data Platform Governance Architect who can bridge the gap between governance ambitions and technical reality, helping us build a scalable, secure, and trusted data platform that enables better decisions across the business.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have helped design, establish, or mature enterprise-scale data platforms and who understand what a well-functioning platform looks like from both a governance and architecture perspective.

About the role | Bridging governance, platform architecture and technology

As our new Data Platform Governance Architect, you will act as the technical bridge between our data governance and data platform teams. Your primary responsibility is to translate governance requirements into clear, actionable technical specifications while ensuring governance stakeholders understand platform capabilities, constraints, and trade-offs.

You will draw on your hands-on experience from data platform architecture, data platform engineering, data management, or governance roles to define robust, implementable governance requirements. You will also help design and implement governance processes and feedback loops. You will work closely with the platform team, which is responsible for implementing the technical solutions.

Your key responsibilities include:

• Defining governance requirements and frameworks for data access, classification, lineage, catalog structures, and tagging taxonomies

• Translating governance, compliance, and security requirements into clear technical specifications and platform controls

• Designing scalable access and operating models, including onboarding, approval workflows, roles, responsibilities, and ownership structures

• Advising on governance capabilities within Databricks, Unity Catalog, and cloud-based identity and access management solutions

• Aligning governance policies with platform implementation and producing governance documentation, access model designs, and process descriptions

• Advising and challenging stakeholders to embed governance into platform processes and enable efficient, governed data product delivery across teams and business domains

You will play a key role in embedding governance into our data platform landscape, working closely with experienced specialists across data, security, architecture, and governance to shape standards and practices that support the long-term strategic use of data throughout the organization. You will help ensure governance and compliance enable scalable data delivery rather than create bottlenecks as platform adoption grows.

About you | Platform architecture mindset and governance credibility

To succeed in this role, you combine strong governance thinking with a solid technical foundation. You understand how modern cloud-based enterprise data platforms are designed, established, and operated because you have helped build, evolve, or govern them in previous roles. You enjoy translating complexity into clarity and can confidently engage with both technical specialists and business stakeholders.

You will be most successful if you:

Must-have qualifications

• Have at least 4 years of experience within data platform architecture, data platform engineering, data governance, data management, or related disciplines, including experience contributing to the design, implementation, or evolution of an enterprise-scale data platform.

• Possess hands-on experience with Databricks and Unity Catalog, including RBAC, governance controls, catalog and schema structures, lineage, classification, tagging, and security capabilities.

• Understand cloud-based identity and access management, including Azure Entra ID, Active Directory, RBAC, ABAC, service principals, and storage permissions, and be able to translate governance requirements into clear, implementable technical specifications.

• Have experience designing and implementing governance models and processes for how data is onboarded, structured, accessed, governed, and delivered across a modern data platform.

• Have experience establishing operating models for data ownership, stewardship, and data product delivery, combined with strong stakeholder management and communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences.

It is an advantage if you

• Have experience from a regulated industry, such as insurance, financial services, or healthcare, and have worked with GDPR, privacy requirements, access governance, or compliance controls within cloud-based data platforms.

• Have experience designing enterprise-wide data classification frameworks, tagging taxonomies, and scalable governance practices, where compliance requirements are embedded into platform capabilities and automated processes.

• Understand modern data architecture and platform automation, including medallion architecture, data products, domain-driven ownership models, infrastructure-as-code, GitLab, Terraform, and CI/CD practices.

• Hold relevant certifications, such as CDMP, DAMA, or Databricks certifications.

You are naturally collaborative, analytical, and pragmatic, with a talent for challenging assumptions and turning complexity into practical solutions. You understand how to balance risk, usability, and business value, embedding governance into the platform to enable trusted data delivery at scale.
